method: Differential whole-file source review against fully read Unix SSE4.1 assembly. All1083 unified-diff lines inspected in1..400/401..800/801..1083 without truncation; unchanged source verified text-identical using SequenceMatcher autojunk disabled. Equivalent lines not independently serial-reread.
findings: Rotate16 replaces pshufb masks with pshuflw/pshufhw immediate0xB1, swapping16-bit halves inside each32-bit word. Rotate8 uses right8/left24 plus XOR of nonoverlapping bit fields. Temporary registers are explicit across unrolled four-input and scalar/two-input loops.

PBLENDW masks replace SSE4.1 word blending using AND/OR:33/CC choose alternating32-bit words,3F/C0 select lower96 versus upper32 bits. Extra spills preserve active XMM2 and intermediate message vectors in two-input permutation.

Counter low/high words are packed via movd and punpckldq instead of pinsrd. Full-block length64 and flags are combined into64-bit scalar then punpcklqdq into compression state. Flags are refreshed each block before packing.

After two-input output, increment mask is loaded then negated from0/-1 to0/1, selecting lane0 or lane2 via scale8 in low/high counter arrays. This replaces blendvps; source assumes boolean increment_counter supplied by caller.

Common group4/2/1 structure,128/64/32-byte output sizes, unaligned16-byte input loads, SysV register saves, stack alignment, first/end flags and full-block caller preconditions remain as previously read SSE4.1 source.

Scalar compression32/64-byte outputs retain full64-byte padded reads. Rotate byte constants are removed, new blend masks appended. Source substitutions alone do not prove parity on SSE2 hardware or establish speed.
limits: No x86 execution, Windows ABI, sanitizer or throughput proof; no upstream production import. Deferred pHash/ASAN untouched.
